title: The Garden of Caerlum Again
premise: Orsen Halloran keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, and has spent years hiding one theft of his own: a memory he took from himself to survive something unspeakable. When the old gods resume answering prayers, the guild's impossible inventory begins waking up — including the memory Orsen stole from King Aldric Caerlum, whose crown is now worn by a hollow thing wearing his face. Guided by Sefa, a priestess who loves him and serves the god he robbed, Orsen must unbind the true king before the impostor completes a rite that will feed every prayer in the realm to the god beneath the mountain. In the end Orsen restores Aldric's memory at the cost of his own hidden past, learning that what he buried was the memory of killing his brother to survive — and that love means carrying grief rather than trading it away.
about_author: Gideon Okafor is a former archivist who claims he left the profession after cataloguing a collection of letters addressed to people who did not yet exist. He writes fantasy about debt, memory, and the arithmetic of love from a house with too many locked drawers.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He audits the Vellum Guild's vaults, cataloguing bottled memories and stranger wares, while concealing his own sealed memory among them. A prayer candle burns that hasn't burned in three hundred years. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The priestess witnesses her neglected god answer a beggar's prayer with terrifying precision, and realizes the old gods are awake again. She is ordered to investigate the guild's connection. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Client with No Face
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A veiled buyer purchases a royal memory — the ledger shows it was sold decades ago by someone with Orsen's own handwriting. He begins hunting his predecessor's records. Emotional beat: unease turning to obsession.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Summoned to court, she prays before King Aldric and watches the blessing slide off him like rain off glass. Something wearing the king answers her anyway. Emotional beat: horror masked as courtesy.

chapters.title: The Guild's Oldest Debt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The guildmaster admits the guild once served the gods as memory-keepers and betrayed them; the waking gods are collecting. Orsen's sealed memory is named as collateral. Emotional beat: betrayal by an institution he trusted.

chapters.title: A Thief and a Priestess
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Orsen and Sefa meet in a shrine at night, each investigating the other, and recognize a shared loneliness. They form a wary alliance over stolen wine. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Memory That Bites
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He attempts to open his own sealed memory and is nearly destroyed by its defenses — something in it screams. Sefa finds him bleeding from the nose, eyes full of a country he doesn't remember. Emotional beat: terror of oneself.

chapters.title: The Rite Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Ancient texts reveal the impostor king is preparing the Unbinding Rite, which would pour every answered prayer into the starving god below. They have until the harvest moon. Emotional beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Road Through the Ash Orchards
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The pair travel toward Caerlum's summer palace, passing villages drunk on answered prayers, worshipping carelessly. Orsen steals a memory to save Sefa's life and hates how easy it feels. Emotional beat: love complicated by his nature.

chapters.title: The Brother I Don't Remember
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She secretly reads Orsen's sealed memory through her god's sight and learns it contains a dead boy and a knife — but says nothing. Emotional beat: the weight of a merciful lie.

chapters.title: Court of Hollow Faces
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Infiltrating the palace, Orsen finds courtiers all bearing faintly identical smiles — memories skimmed by the crown-thing. He locates the true Aldric's memory vial in the treasury of prayers. Emotional beat: revulsion and resolve.

chapters.title: The God Who Was Robbed
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Her god manifests and demands payment for the guild's ancient theft — offering to forgive everything if Sefa delivers Orsen's sealed memory instead. Emotional beat: duty sharpened into a blade against love.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The rite begins early; the sky bruises violet. Orsen and Sefa flee the palace with the vial as the impostor's hunters — men with no memories at all — close in. Emotional beat: desperate flight.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Captured briefly by the impostor, Orsen is shown his own future: a throne of forgotten things, painless and empty. He escapes when the crown-thing falters at a memory of genuine love. Emotional beat: temptation refused.

chapters.title: The Confession at the Ford
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Cornered, Sefa confesses she read his sealed memory. Orsen's rage nearly breaks the alliance; she argues that survival bought with forgetting isn't survival. Emotional beat: love tested by truth.

chapters.title: The Knife in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He finally opens the memory: as children, he killed his brother to escape the guild's tithe-takers, then stole the memory to keep living. Grief floods back whole. Emotional beat: devastation, and strange relief.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen offers his reopened memory to his god as payment for the guild's debt, choosing to carry his guilt rather than trade it. The god, moved by an honest accounting, accepts a lesser price. Emotional beat: absolution through ownership.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the mountain's heart, the impostor feeds the rite. Sefa channels her god's voice while Orsen pours Aldric's memory into the crown-thing's mouth. The true king wakes inside the counterfeit. Emotional beat: climax — everything staked at once.

chapters.title: A King Made Whole
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Aldric, restored and grieving his lost decades, executes no one; he forgives the court and dissolves the guild's charter. The starving god, fed by honest mourning instead of stolen prayer, sleeps again. Emotional beat: mercy as victory.

chapters.title: The Price, Tallied
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen resigns as keeper of ledgers, burning the inventory of stolen memories so every thief's victims can grieve and heal. Some memories return to screaming owners; he stays to witness each one. Emotional beat: penance freely chosen.

chapters.title: Where Prayers Go Now
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The gods grow quiet again, answering only rarely. Sefa rebuilds her shrine around listening rather than asking, and chooses Orsen over doctrine when her order demands his exile. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved.

chapters.title: The Garden of Caerlum Again
chapters.summary: Shared POV. In the ruined royal garden, now blooming wild, Orsen plants a tree for his brother and tells Sefa the whole story aloud, start to finish. Memory kept, not traded, becomes their covenant. Emotional beat: grief and love rooted together.
